vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in FreeType, specifically within its CID font loader. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by tricking a user into opening content that embeds or references a specially crafted CID-keyed font. This crafted font can cause repeated allocations and decryptions of subroutine data across multiple font dictionaries, leading to excessive memory and CPU consumption. This can result in a denial of service (DoS) for the application or service processing the font, potentially causing it to hang or terminate.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. The next image rebuild includes the fixed Ubuntu package 2.13.2+dfsg-1ubuntu0.2.

ratings.justification: No shipped program opens fonts with the system FreeType; the JVM uses its bundled copy and Liquibase never renders text.

analysis.detail: Exploitation needs the process to open an attacker-supplied CID-keyed font through the system FreeType. In the image the system libfreetype.so.6 is linked only by libfontconfig and the fc-* command-line tools. The JVM's font code (libfontmanager.so) links the FreeType copy bundled with the Temurin JDK, not the system one, and Liquibase never loads a font: it is a headless CLI whose only AWT use is GraphicsEnvironment.isHeadless() and Desktop.browse() in the report writer, neither of which initialises the font stack. Ubuntu fixed the package in 2.13.2+dfsg-1ubuntu0.2 (USN-8881-1); the next image rebuild picks it up.

vulnerabilities.description: An integer overflow in the tt_var_load_item_variation_store function of the Freetype library in versions 2.13.2 and 2.13.3 may allow for an out of bounds read operation when parsing HVAR/VVAR/MVAR tables in OpenType variable fonts. This issue is fixed in version 2.14.2.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No font in the Liquibase Secure image is a variable font.

ratings.justification: The system FreeType, loaded only through fontconfig, parses the variation tables only for variable fonts, and the image's only fonts are static TrueType fonts.

analysis.detail: The integer overflow is in FreeType's tt_var_load_item_variation_store and is reached only while FreeType parses the HVAR, VVAR or MVAR table of an OpenType variable font. libfreetype6 is an inherited base-image library. The JDK rasterises text with its own bundled FreeType, not this one. The system FreeType reaches the JVM only indirectly: when Java initialises its font subsystem, the JDK loads libfontconfig, which uses the system FreeType to read the font files it lists, from the system font directories, owned by root, and from per-user font directories that only the account running Liquibase can write. The image's only installed fonts are the DejaVu TrueType fonts under /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu, which are static fonts with no fvar, HVAR, VVAR or MVAR table. The fc-* tools that also link it are never run by the image. The container entrypoint runs only the Liquibase CLI and the optional lpm helper, a statically linked Go binary. Ubuntu fixed this in 2.13.2+dfsg-1ubuntu0.1 (noble); the jammy package (2.11.1) does not contain the code. Docker images 5.0.2 through 5.1.0 carry the unfixed 2.13.2+dfsg-1build3; 5.1.1 and later carry 2.13.2+dfsg-1ubuntu0.1.
